title: Ancient Numerals Converter
description: Convert decimal numbers to Roman, Egyptian hieroglyphic, Babylonian cuneiform and Mayan numerals — with Roman numerals also decoded back to decimal.
howto: Type a decimal number (1–3999 for full Roman support).
Press Convert to see it in all four ancient systems at once.
Or switch to Roman → decimal mode and paste numerals like MCMXCIV to decode.
Each system shows how its symbols add up to your number.

faqs.q: How do Egyptian hieroglyphic numerals work?
faqs.a: Purely additive: 𓏺=1, 𓎆=10, 𓍢=100, 𓆼=1,000, 𓂭=10,000, 𓆐=100,000, 𓁨=1,000,000. The number 234 is written as 𓍢𓍢𓎆𓎆𓎆𓏺𓏺𓏺𓏺 — symbols are simply repeated and added.
Base 60 (sexagesimal): each position holds 0–59 written with 𒁹 (1) and 𒌋 (10), positions separated here by spaces. 75 = 1·60 + 15, shown as 𒁹 𒌋𒁹𒁹𒁹𒁹𒁹.
Base 20 (vigesimal): each position holds 0–19 using dots (1) and bars (5), written vertically. Here positions are shown top (highest) to bottom, separated by spaces.
